products.summary: Hindu temple ERP: poojas, sevas, vazhipadu, donations, hundi, halls, festivals and audit-grade fund accounting, with or without Odoo Accounting
products.description:
Temple Management System

Poojas, sevas, vazhipadu, donations, hundi, halls and festivals with audit-grade fund accounting, for Odoo 20 Community

Run the whole temple office in Odoo: a fast counter that prints receipts in seconds, a pooja register for the priests, devotees and families with their nakshatra, donations into the right funds, hundi opening and double counting with witnesses, hall bookings, festivals with sponsorships, memberships and dues. Every rupee received or spent becomes a balanced posting in the temple ledger, and a real journal entry when Odoo Accounting is installed.

Odoo 20 Community Works with or without Odoo Accounting Depends only on Base and Discuss 97 automated tests

A counter built for queues

Find the devotee by phone, type AR*2 or tap a tile, take cash, UPI, card or cheque and print. Family members and their stars are one click away. One call creates the booking, the gapless receipt number, the payment and the posting.

Money handled in the open

Cash sessions with denomination counts and verified variances. Hundi boxes opened before witnesses, counted by two teams, verified by a third person and posted by a fourth. Every sensitive action lands in a tamper-evident audit log.

Accounts your auditor accepts

Restricted, designated and corpus funds kept apart. Advance bookings held as liabilities until the pooja is performed. Income & Expenditure with fund columns, Receipts & Payments, trial balance and donor-deduction receipts.

Counter & receipts

  • Keyboard-first counter screen: search by phone, devotee ID or name, short codes with quantities (AR*3), Ctrl+Enter to confirm and print, walk-in devotees without a record.
  • Several poojas, beneficiaries, stars, dates and a donation on one receipt; split payments across cash, UPI, card, cheque/DD and bank transfer with references.
  • Gapless receipt numbering per counter and financial year; duplicate-click protection; reprints counted. Cashiers can cancel their own receipt only within a short window in an open session; after that only an accountant can, always with a reason, and the posting is reversed.
  • A5 or thermal receipts with amount in words, trust registration, donor-deduction text and a QR verification code. Paper receipt books can be entered later with their own numbers.
  • Counter sessions: cash counted by denomination at close, variance above your limit needs a manager, sessions verified by someone other than the cashier.

Printed receipt

Counter session report

Poojas, sevas & vazhipadu

  • Offerings per deity and shrine with fixed, minimum or open prices, short codes, slots, capacity per day, lead time, how far ahead they can be booked and on which days they are performed.
  • Ask for nakshatra, gotra or the beneficiary's name only where the offering needs it.
  • Pooja Register for the day: who it is offered for, star, deity, priest and status. Priests mark poojas performed; the coordinator can auto-assign qualified priests, balancing the load.
  • Advance bookings are held as an advance and recognised as income on the day of the pooja. Cancellation policies refund by notice period; recurring bookings for regular devotees.
  • Share splits: part of a seva's price can go to a supplier or priest share instead of temple income.
  • One calendar for poojas, festivals and hall bookings, filterable by deity.

Devotees & families

  • Devotee ID, name in local script, nakshatra (rashi and gotra if you use them), preferred deity, family and relation to the head.
  • Bookings, donations and receipts of each devotee one click away; book a pooja or receive a donation straight from the record.
  • Consent per channel (email, SMS, WhatsApp); PAN and other sensitive data visible only to authorised staff and shown masked elsewhere.
  • Devotee import with duplicate detection, personal data export and anonymisation on request.

Donations & funds

  • Donation types mapped to funds: general, deity, annadanam, building, festival, charity and corpus.
  • Restricted funds are released to income only when they are spent; corpus donations need the donor's written direction and are never treated as income.
  • Receipts state eligibility for deduction under s.354 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly s.80G) with your approval number. Cash donations above the deduction limit are not marked eligible, and cash receipts above the maximum you set are refused.
  • Donor statement data for Form 113 (formerly Form 10BD).
  • Fund balances on the dashboard and fund-to-fund transfers that need a manager and a board resolution reference.

Hundi collections

  • Each hundi box with its current seal number; a collection cannot be opened without seal numbers and the minimum number of witnesses.
  • Two counting teams count independently by denomination. Counts are frozen once submitted; a difference needs a note and an administrator.
  • A counting-team member cannot verify, and the verifier cannot post. Purpose hundis (for example annadanam) credit their fund.
  • Foreign currency in custody and a valuables register for gold, silver and other offerings found in the box.
  • Deposit slip to the bank, new seal numbers, and printed counting proceedings for the witnesses to sign.

Counting proceedings with both teams' counts

Halls & facilities

  • Kalyana mandapam, dining hall, meeting rooms: hourly, half-day or daily rates, weekday and weekend prices, refundable deposits, minimum advance and a cleaning buffer between bookings.
  • Double bookings are refused, including the buffer; expired quotations free the slot; maintenance blocks.
  • Quotation, approval, advance, deposit, check-in, completion and billing. GST on hall rent above the exemption threshold.
  • Cancellation keeps the fee you set and refunds the rest; deposits are refunded after the event, less any damage.

Booking confirmation with GST, deposit and advance

Festivals & sponsorships

  • Festivals with a day-by-day programme; collections during the festival are tagged to it automatically.
  • Budget, income, expenses and net result per festival.
  • Sponsorship packages (ubayam, annadanam, nadaswaram, deepalankaram) with a limit on sponsors and payment at the counter.

Memberships, dues & expenses

  • Annual and life memberships; life membership fees can go to the corpus. Renewal dues are generated automatically.
  • Recurring monthly contributions; overdue dues are flagged and can be collected at the counter in one receipt. Waivers need a manager.
  • Expenses with approval limits per category: submitted, approved by a manager, paid from cash or bank, or booked to a payee. Paying from a restricted fund releases it.
  • Bank deposits of counter cash and cheques, cheque bounce handling, and UPI/card settlements with gateway charges.

Fund accounting & reports

  • A ready chart of ledger heads for temples: income by offering, funds, advances, deposits, clearing accounts for each payment method.
  • Every financial event goes through configurable posting rules and becomes one balanced, idempotent posting: it can never be posted twice, and corrections are reversals, not edits.
  • Period lock and backdating only for authorised users.
  • Temple Ledger pivot, Daily Collection Report per counter and payment method, Trial Balance, Income & Expenditure with unrestricted and restricted fund columns, Receipts & Payments.

Income & Expenditure (fund columns)

Receipts & Payments

Daily Collection Report

With or without Odoo Accounting

Small temples run on the built-in temple ledger alone. When the Invoicing/Accounting app is installed, an accountant activates the integration with a cut-over date: missing accounts and four journals (collections, hundi, expenses, adjustments) are created, and from then on every temple posting becomes a posted Odoo journal entry, with an analytic account per restricted fund. Reversals follow automatically, sync errors never block the counter and are retried, and Odoo lock dates are respected.

Roles, audit & settings

  • Roles: Front Office, Counter Staff, Coordinator, Accountant, Manager, Administrator, Priest, Auditor (read-only) and Trustee, plus separate rights for sensitive personal data and backdating.
  • Append-only audit log of receipts, postings, approvals, cancellations and session closures, with an optional SHA-256 hash chain that is extended every few minutes and verified weekly.
  • Notifications by email through Odoo, or SMS and WhatsApp through any HTTP gateway you configure; consent is checked before sending. Reminders for advance poojas and dues.
  • Multi-company ready, with several shrines, deities and counters per temple.

Technical notes

  • Odoo 20.0 Community (PostgreSQL 16 or later). Depends only on Base and Discuss (mail); Invoicing/Accounting is optional. No Enterprise or paid third-party modules.
  • Built for Indian temples (rupee denominations, GST on hall rent, Income-tax Act 2025 references), and configurable for temples elsewhere: nakshatra, rashi and gotra fields can be switched off.
  • Demo data with a sample temple, deities, offerings, devotees and users. Fully translatable.
  • 97 automated tests cover the counter, accounting, funds, hundi, halls, festivals, memberships, notifications, reports and security.
